newsitem.title: FRANCE: French savings bank group sees restructuring role.
newsitem.headline: French savings bank group sees restructuring role.

text.p: French savings bank grouping Caisses d'Epargne intends to play an active role in the restructuring of the banking sector, and most of its member savings banks believe that growth by acquisition is inevitable, Rene Barberye, head of the central board of the Caisses grouping, said on Tuesday.
"We cannot stand on the sidelines of a restructuring of the French banking landscape. Quite the contrary, we want to be a participant," Barberye said in an interview in daily Le Monde.
"I believe the most of the heads of the Caisses d'Epargne are convinced that we will have to grow by acquisition sooner or later," he was quoted as saying in the afternoon daily.

The Caisses grouping said on Monday evening it was not going to bid for Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC), which is being privatised via the sale of 67 percent by state insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales GAN.
Barberye said the CIC privatisation tender had given his grouping the opportunity to carry out a full bid assessment for the first time and that this would prove useful for the future.

He said his group had not backed down under pressure either from the public authorities or from the AFB French banking association, whose mainly commercial bank members had attacked the idea of a CIC sale to a savings bank grouping.

Explaining the reasons for not making an offer, Barberye highlighted that CIC was an operation with a primarily wealthier and heavily corporate clientele, while the Caisses had a less well-off clientele and an image as a social banker.

The deadline for bids for CIC expired at 1600 GMT on Monday with no word from the finance ministry on the candidates. Le Monde said on Monday BNP had decided to enter the bidding but the bank declined to say more than that all candidates were obliged to keep their position out of the public.
Societe Generale is tipped as the other bidder.
